title: First ai trading bot iteration
author: Tylerd62
selftext:
Hey all, long time lurker. I've been day trading futures for a while (mostly prop accounts) and I finally sat down to turn one of my discretionary setups into something mechanical so I can actually test it instead of going off gut feel. This is my first time doing anything like this, so I'd appreciate opinions from people who've been through it.  
**The setup (5 min chart):**  
Opening range is 6:00-6:15 AM CT

Wait for a clean break out of the range. Price has to actually run away from the level (I'm using 1.5x ATR of separation) or it doesn't count

First retest of the broken level only. If the level holds and I get a candle closing back in the breakout direction, I enter. It's a continuation trade, not a fade

If the confirmation candle is a huge displacement candle (over 2x ATR, or entry more than 1x ATR from the level), I skip it and wait for price to come back again

One trade a day max, no new entries after noon CT, flat by 3 PM CT

Stop goes at the recent swing low/high and only triggers on a candle close past it

Take 50% off at 1.5R, move stop to breakeven (hard stop), let the rest run to 2R

**What I've found so far:**  
I started with just the chart history TradingView loads and it looked great. I ran it across about 10 instruments (forex pairs, silver, crude, gold, AAPL, micro dow) and got around 147 trades at roughly +0.22R per trade before costs, with 8 of the 10 positive. I got pretty excited lol.  
Then I ran deep backtests and it humbled me quick:  
EUR/USD last 365 days: PF 1.40, about +29R. Great

EUR/USD 2013-2026: PF 1.07 before costs. Once I added about 1 pip of spread per trade it went negative. My stops are tight enough that the spread eats most of the edge

EUR/USD back to 2007: basically breakeven, and it sat underwater for like a decade

Silver 2013-2026: PF about 1.15 before costs, but most of the profit came from 2013-2017 and this year's rally. It slowly bled in between

So my read is it makes money in trending, volatile periods and slowly bleeds in chop. I'm dropping forex because of costs and focusing on micro gold and silver.  
**What I'm doing next:**  
I'm tagging every trade with market conditions known before entry (daily ATR percentile, a 20-day efficiency ratio, with/against the daily 50 SMA, and today's opening range size vs its 20-day average). Then I'll export the trade list and see which conditions the losers cluster in. The plan is to pick any filter using 2002-2020 data and then check it on 2021-2026 without changing anything. If it doesn't hold up, I toss it. I'm also thinking about fading failed breakouts on choppy days instead of sitting out.  
**Questions for you guys:**  
Is a regime filter like this legit, or am I just going to curve fit myself into a false sense of security? How do you all guard against that?

For those running ORB-type stuff on 5 min, do you just accept costs are brutal on tight stops, or did you move to 15 min or wider structure?

Partial at 1.5R plus runner vs full exit: has anyone found one clearly better for this kind of setup? My small sample says it depends on the instrument (gold doesn't follow through, silver runs).

Is TradingView deep backtesting good enough for this, or should I be moving to Python or something else?

Anything obvious I'm missing? Open to any criticism. I'd rather find the holes now than with real money.

Appreciate anyone who read all this.  
**TL;DR:** First time turning my ORB continuation setup into a backtestable system. Looks great short term, has a thin edge long term that dies with costs on forex. Working on regime filters with an out-of-sample check and moving to futures. Looking for feedback on my process.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
6:00-6:15 CT is well before the 8:30 cash open on index futures, so that range is built on overnight volume and will behave differently from one around the open. worth testing both, the setup might only work in one of them.

before coding anything I'd pin down when a retest stops counting. if price breaks out and runs without coming back, that's a skipped trade, and if the rule doesn't say how long you wait you'll end up quietly picking the retests that worked. write the timeout into the rule, within N bars or it's void, and count how many breakouts never retest at all. that count tells you a lot about whether the edge is in the break or in the retest.

replies.author: Tylerd62
replies.body: Thank you I will keep that in mind!

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: good luck with it. the 6:00 range vs one built around the 8:30 open is the first test I'd run.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: anytime. post the next iteration when it's running, would like to see how it changes.
